rtl_snippet: always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrst_n) begin

fix.rationale:
The startpoint (_124902_, DFF at uart_rx.v:170 = the fsm_state register) fans out combinationally into uart_rx_valid, which is then consumed off-module by an async-FIFO write-pointer register in wptr_full.v (the endpoint DFFR). RETIME is not available: there is no register sitting inside this combinational cloud that could be slid to rebalance it — the only sequential elements on the path are the fsm_state source flop and the destination flop in a different module, and moving either would change latency/interface, not just timing. PIPELINE was rejected because it is strictly worse than an available zero-cost option: inserting a stage would delay uart_rx_valid (and therefore uart_rx_data and the FIFO push) by a cycle and require re-balancing every reconvergent consumer of uart_rx_valid, none of which I can verify from this scope.

RESTRUCTURE is available and sufficient. In the existing RTL, `fsm_state == FSM_STOP` is applied twice in series on the same signal: once inside `next_bit` (`... || (fsm_state==FSM_STOP && cycle_counter==CYCLES_PER_BIT/2)`), and again at the top level of `uart_rx_valid = fsm_state==FSM_STOP && next_bit`. Algebraically, for any boolean x and terms A ("cycle_full"), B ("cycle_half"): `x && (A || (x && B)) == x && (A || B)` (trivially true for x=0, and for x=1 both sides reduce to A||B). I introduced named sub-signals `fsm_is_stop`, `cycle_full`, `cycle_half` (same comparisons as before, just shared instead of recomputed) and rewrote `uart_rx_valid` as `fsm_is_stop && (cycle_full || cycle_half)`. This is provably identical for every input combination, but it removes one AND level of fsm_state's own fan-in from the critical path: previously fsm_state had to propagate through an AND, then an OR, then a second AND before reaching uart_rx_valid; now `cycle_full || cycle_half` can settle independently of fsm_state, leaving only a single AND gate between fsm_is_stop and uart_rx_valid. `next_bit` itself is left functionally and structurally equivalent (same expression, just reusing the shared cycle_full/cycle_half/fsm_is_stop wires) so every other consumer of `next_bit` (n_fsm_state case, p_bit_counter, p_cycle_counter) sees bit-identical timing and value — no reconvergent path needs rebalancing since nothing downstream changed in cycle count or value, only the gate depth feeding uart_rx_valid from fsm_state.

I could not confirm from the given RTL alone how much of the reported 0.940ns is inside uart_rx.v versus inside wptr_full.v (12 of 14 cells are unattributed, and three trailing XOR2_X1 stages plus a NOR3_X1 look characteristic of gray-code pointer/full-flag logic in the async FIFO, not of anything in uart_rx.v). I'm not filing that as the primary fix, however, since this restructuring is a legitimate, provable, zero-cost reduction of real redundant logic on this exact path and should be applied regardless of whether additional delay also lives in wptr_full.v.

out_of_scope_fix.reason: The last few cells on the path (three XOR2_X1 stages feeding a NOR3_X1 into the DFFR_X1 endpoint at wptr_full.v:52) are consistent with gray-code pointer computation and full-flag comparison inside the async FIFO's write-pointer module, not with any logic present in uart_rx.v; if slack remains negative after the uart_rx.v restructuring, that module's pointer/compare logic should be inspected for a similar redundant-recompute or retimeable register.
